author: tickeron_community
selftext:
**AI-driven trading analysis tracks JPM, BAC, NVDA, GOOG, AVGO, META, and AMD using a systematic 60-minute trading approach.**

 AI-driven market analysis and systematic trading are increasingly being applied to large-cap technology and financial stocks. Tickeron's latest trading results cover JPM, BAC, NVDA, GOOG, AVGO, META and AMD through an AI Trading Agent using a 60-minute approach.  
  
**Announcement Summary**  
  
[Tickeron](https://tickeron.com/) has reported historical performance data from an [AI Trading Agent](https://tickeron.com/app/ai-robots/trending-robots/) covering seven widely followed technology and financial tickers.

* 119-day reporting period from September 24, 2025 to September 23, 2026
* $24,460.85 in closed-trade net profit based on $20,000 per trade
* 70 closed trades, including 46 profitable trades
* 95.65% reported annualized return
* 3.09 profit factor and 1.20 Sharpe ratio

  
The reported results provide a historical view of how algorithmic trading systems can be applied across a diversified group of major stocks. The data also shows an absolute drawdown of $6,687.55, highlighting the importance of a risk-aware approach when evaluating systematic strategies.  
  
Tickeron's technology combines AI-driven financial analysis with algorithmic trading tools designed to process market information and identify trading opportunities. Its Financial Learning Models (FLMs) are used as part of the platform's broader AI infrastructure.  
  
Tickeron has recently expanded its computing infrastructure and increased the capabilities of its Financial Learning Models (FLMs) to support more sophisticated AI analysis and trading automation.

Additional information on the tracked securities and market tools is available through Tickeron's pages for AMD, NVDA, and JPM.

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
How does the 119-day reporting period reconcile with September 24, 2025 through September 23, 2026? That needs clarification before interpreting the AI Trading Agent's 95.65% annualized return.

Also, $20,000 per trade doesn't establish the account capital required if positions overlap across the seven tickers. Could you show the return calculation's capital denominator and whether the $6,687.55 drawdown includes unrealized losses? I can't inspect the linked image from this snapshot, so those definitions would need checking in the underlying report.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the dates don't match the label. September 24 2025 to September 23 2026 is a full year, not 119 days, so either the period is wrong or the annualized figure is scaling up a third of a year. and $20k per trade across seven tickers says nothing about how much capital was actually tied up at once, which is what any percentage needs underneath it.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body:
The headline number is doing a lot of work here — 95.65% "annualized return" is extrapolated from a 119-day window, and annualizing a partial-year result like that overstates what you'd actually expect to hold over a full year, especially once you account for the $6,687.55 drawdown sitting inside that same short window. 70 closed trades across seven large-cap names that are already fairly correlated with each other (JPM/BAC move together, the mega-cap tech names move together) isn't really the diversified sample the framing suggests — it's a small number of trades concentrated in two correlated baskets, which makes the Sharpe (1.20) and profit factor (3.09) numbers less robust than they look at a glance.

Worth also noting this reads as a paid placement rather than independent reporting — the links carry an affiliate tag (`via=serhii-bondarenko`) alongside the discounted-pricing pitch for the paid tiers, which is fine as disclosure goes, but it means the performance stats are self-reported by the platform selling the product, not independently verified. That doesn't make the numbers false, just worth treating the way you'd treat any vendor-supplied backtest: ask whether this is live/paper trading over that period or a historical backtest run after the fact, since those get conflated constantly in this space and the difference matters a lot for whether the result is repeatable going forward.

If you're evaluating AI trading tools on the signal-quality side rather than the marketing side, that's the layer EventTrader's built around — event-driven data feeding into strategies rather than a black-box "robot" you're trusting on faith, which is a useful contrast when you're trying to judge whether a result like this is a real edge or a well-timed backtest.
